entities.summary: Sebestyén Tinódi Lantos was a 16th-century Hungarian lyricist, epic poet, political historian, and minstrel who played a crucial role in the cultural and literary Renaissance of Eastern Europe during the Late Middle Ages. His works, including the epic poem “Miklós Zrínyi’s War Poems”, showcased his mastery of the Hungarian language and his ability to tell stories of national identity and struggle. Lantos was also a key figure in the Hungarian Reformation, using his writing to advocate for religious reform and challenge the authority of the Catholic Church. His legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing later generations of Hungarian writers and thinkers. Lantos's work continues to be celebrated for its poetic beauty and historical significance, offering insights into the complex cultural and religious landscape of Late Medieval Europe.
